body:
WHAT
MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers are external programs that expose tools over JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout. At boot, MAGENTRA starts each server listed in settings.mcpServers, asks it for its tools, and registers each one as a normal tool named mcp__<server>__<tool>. A tool call is forwarded to the server; a result with isError becomes a tool error; an image part in the result is replaced with the text '[image content omitted]'.

WHY
Without it, users cannot extend the agent with third-party tools, and a misbehaving server would either vanish silently or crash the whole session instead of producing a visible warning or a tool error.

WHERE
engine/core/src/integrations/mcp.ts — class McpClient (connect(), initialize(), listTools(), callTool() with the image-to-note mapping and McpToolError throw, request() with REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS/CALL_TIMEOUT_MS, onData()/onLine() newline-delimited parsing, fail(), close()); createMcpTools() (validates with mcpServerConfigSchema, collects warnings instead of throwing); makeMcpTool() (permissionClass 'network', permissive zod inputSchema plus rawInputSchema, execute() maps McpToolError to isError:true). Boot wiring: engine/host/src/bootstrap.ts registers mcp.tools into createDefaultRegistry() and forwards mcp.warnings.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Spawn a small fake stdio MCP server script (node) that answers initialize and tools/list with one tool 'echo'; call createMcpTools({ srv: { command: 'node', args: [script] } }) and assert exactly one tool named 'mcp__srv__echo' with rawInputSchema equal to the advertised schema and no warnings.
2. Call that tool's execute() with { text: 'hi' } where the fake server returns content [{type:'text',text:'hi'},{type:'image',data:'...'}]; assert content is 'hi\n[image content omitted]' and isError is undefined.
3. Make the fake server return { isError: true, content: [{type:'text',text:'boom'}] }; assert execute() resolves (does not throw) with { content: 'boom', isError: true }.
4. Pass a config missing 'command' and another whose command does not exist; assert createMcpTools returns zero tools and two warnings mentioning the server names, and never rejects.
5. Kill the fake server process after connect and call the tool; assert execute() resolves with isError:true and a message containing 'process exited', and that a pending request rejects rather than hanging (use a short timeoutMs).
